title: Tor base change along a flat coefficient extension
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let R\to A\to B be homomorphisms of commutative rings, and assume that B is flat as an A-module. For every R-module M and every n\ge 0, the canonical coefficient-base-change map $$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,A)\otimes_A B\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,B)$$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, if A\to B is faithfully flat and $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,B)=0$, then $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,A)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 00M8 (algebra-lemma-flat-base-change-tor), whose free-resolution proof applies verbatim with a fixed base ring R and flat coefficient extension A -> B.

proof.text: Choose a free resolution $P_\bullet\to M$ over $R$: existence follows, for example, by applying [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split] to $0\to M\xrightarrow{1}M\to0\to0$ and retaining its first resolution. Put $C_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_R A$ and $D_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_R B$, with $C_{-1}=D_{-1}=0$ (the augmentations to $M$ are not included in these complexes). By [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], $H_n(C_\bullet)=\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)$ and $H_n(D_\bullet)=\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)$ for all $n\ge0$. Multiplication on the second tensor factor makes $C_\bullet$ a complex of $A$-modules and $D_\bullet$ a complex of $B$-modules; these actions induce the coefficient actions on Tor.

source.place: Tag 00LY (algebra-section-tor), resolution definition; Tag 065P (algebra-lemma-reverse-long-exact-seq-ext), free resolutions of a short exact sequence

proof.text:
Write $g:A\to B$ for the coefficient map. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives mutually inverse $B$-linear maps in each degree
$$\theta_j:(P_j\otimes_R A)\otimes_A B\longrightarrow P_j\otimes_R B,\quad(p\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto p\otimes g(a)b,$$
$$\eta_j:p\otimes b\longmapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes b.$$
The $R$-balancing relation holds because the two maps $R\to B$ agree, and the $A$-balancing relation holds because $g(aa')b=g(a)g(a')b$. The composites are identities on generators: $\theta_j\eta_j(p\otimes b)=p\otimes b$ and $\eta_j\theta_j((p\otimes a)\otimes b)=(p\otimes1)\otimes g(a)b=(p\otimes a)\otimes b$. Both differential composites send $(p\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $d_P(p)\otimes g(a)b$. Thus $\theta:C_\bullet\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}D_\bullet$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

source.place: Tag 00M8 (algebra-lemma-flat-base-change-tor), tensor-complex identification in the free-resolution proof, with fixed base R

proof.text:
Since $B$ is flat over $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes $F=-\otimes_A B:\operatorname{Mod}_A\to\operatorname{Mod}_B$ exact: apply its assertion to each three-term part of a short exact sequence, including the zeros at its ends. Tensor is additive by its defining formula on maps. Apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](c) to $C_{n+1}\to C_n\to C_{n-1}$ for each $n\ge0$. Its inverse comparison gives
$$\kappa_n:H_n(C_\bullet)\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n(C_\bullet\otimes_A B).$$
The cited statement says that this comparison is induced by cycles and their quotient by boundaries: if $z\in\ker d_{C,n}$, then $\kappa_n([z]\otimes b)=[z\otimes b]$. There is no boundedness assumption; only these three terms are used, including $C_{-1}=0$ for $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 010N (homology-lemma-exact-functor), exact functors and kernels/cokernels; tensor exactness is algebra Tag 00HD (algebra-lemma-flat)

proof.text:
Compose $\kappa_n$ with $H_n(\theta)$. In the Tor identifications of step 1 this is a $B$-linear isomorphism from $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)\otimes_A B$ to $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)$. To identify the map, let $z=\sum_i p_i\otimes a_i$ be a cycle in $C_n$. The composite sends
$$[z]\otimes b\longmapsto\left[\sum_i p_i\otimes g(a_i)b\right].$$
By functoriality in the coefficient module in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], the map $A\to B$ induces $[z]\mapsto[\sum_i p_i\otimes g(a_i)]$. Its $B$-linear extension across tensor with $B$ gives exactly the displayed formula, hence the canonical coefficient-base-change map. Equality on these generators proves equality of the maps by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the isomorphism therefore proves the assertion for the specified map, not just an abstract isomorphism of the modules.

source.place: Tag 00LY (algebra-section-tor), functoriality in the second variable; Tag 00M8 (algebra-lemma-flat-base-change-tor), natural comparison on a resolution

proof.text: Now assume $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)=0$. Put $T=\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)$. The proved isomorphism gives $T\otimes_A B=0$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the switch isomorphism $B\otimes_A T\cong T\otimes_A B$, $b\otimes t\mapsto t\otimes b$, whose inverse is the same switch. Thus tensoring the complex $0\to T\to0$ on the left with $B$ produces an exact zero complex. By the reflection of exactness in [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], $0\to T\to0$ is exact at $T$. Its kernel there is $T$ and its image is $0$, so $T=0$, as required.

source.place: Tag 00HB (algebra-definition-flat), items (2) and (4), applied to the complex 0 -> T -> 0

split_report.summary: Proved fixed-base coefficient change using an R-free resolution, an explicit tensor-complex isomorphism, flat tensor exactness and the existing exact-functor homology comparison. Identified the resulting isomorphism on cycle representatives with the canonical coefficient map, including n=0, and deduced faithful-flat vanishing from reflection of exactness. No new nodes. Clarified that Stacks 00M8 is the model proof, not the literal fixed-base statement.

No change to the contracting-correspondence unit route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q38-e3dabe9f1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all five steps against the cited statements and Stacks 00M8 (label lemma-flat-base-change-tor, line 18735), 00LY, 00HD, 00HB, 010N and 065P. 00M8 changes the base ring, while this item fixes R and changes only the coefficient A->B; proof_origin correctly records the proof as an agent adaptation. The statement is true and needs no flatness of A or B over R. Small cases agree: Z/2 with Z->Q; Z/4->Z/4[x], where both sides are (Z/2)[x]; and n=0. Step 1 gets a free resolution by applying the free-resolution lemma to 0->M->M->0->0, which is valid. Step 2 (the termwise isomorphism (P(x)A)(x)_A B = P(x)B) is elementary, with R- and A-balancing checked. Step 3 combines the Mathlib leaves on flat tensor exactness and clause (c) of the exact-functor homology lemma; that clause gives the cycle-induced comparison [z](x)b -> [z(x)b] with no boundedness assumption. Step 4 identifies the composite with the B-linear extension of Tor(M,g), so the stated map is the isomorphism. Step 5 proves T=0 from the faithful-flatness definition applied to 0->T->0. There are no new nodes. No existing node duplicates the item: the closest candidates (tor-one-surjective-flat-middle, flat-scalar-extension-tor-comparison, tor-localization-on-spec) differ. Every cited node is a definition, a Mathlib leaf or a Lean-closed node, so there is no route departure and no tool_uses. Changes: none. Note for the maintainer: the maintainer-owned source.place still says the 00M8 proof 'applies verbatim' and would read better as 'adapted'.
